name: claude-skills
note: Generated by scripts/sync.py from plugins/ and SOURCES.json. Do not edit by hand.

plugins.name: agent-identity-governance
plugins.description: Nine skills that treat AI agents, service principals, workload identities, API keys and MCP connectors as identities with an inventory, owners, recertification, expiry and an off switch: one inventory across Entra ID, AWS IAM, GitHub and a hand-kept register; a review of Entra agent identities; quarterly recertification sheets per owner; an expiry radar for secrets, certificates, keys and tokens; a register check for MCP servers and connectors; a timeline of one agent's actions from audit exports; a kill switch runbook with a coverage check; a leaked credential response pack with hashed evidence; and a hash chain that makes an agent audit log tamper-evident and shows actions it never recorded. Standard-library scripts over saved exports, no network.

plugins.name: agent-security
plugins.description: Security skills for LLM agents: threat model a codebase, audit agent configuration, review MCP servers, trace prompt injection to tool calls, check consequential tools for human approval gates, look up incident precedents, run security evals, scan with Semgrep, and review agent session logs for injection, misuse, egress and loops. Includes guard hooks for Bash and an optional incident-database MCP server.

plugins.name: aws-security
plugins.description: AWS security skills for Claude Code: read-only account audit, SCP guardrail builder and linter, landing zone blast-radius design, IAM least-privilege review, Security Hub and GuardDuty triage, least-privilege access for AI agents with a kill switch, incident response runbooks, spend guardrails, a sandbox OU guardrail pack an audit of what an agent role session did, from CloudTrail, and a mapper from failing Security Hub controls to the SCPs, settings and IaC checks that prevent them. Scripts are standard-library Python and work offline on specs and saved aws CLI output.

plugins.name: cc-setup-tooling
plugins.description: Fourteen skills that keep a Claude Code setup safe and tidy: review a third-party skill or plugin before installing it (skill-scan-gate, cc-plugin-lock and an offline inventory), lint SKILL.md front matter and fix its quoting, score descriptions against labelled prompts, estimate what a project loads on every turn, merge least-privilege permission rules and test them with claude-perm-sim, review the sandbox settings across scopes and flag what leaves it open, list the tool calls that would stop an unattended run on a permission prompt, show what each subagent can reach, add up the API usage in session transcripts and show which part moved, count shell commands that failed because of zsh, PowerShell or the Windows length limit, check what each compaction summary dropped, scaffold and test hooks with cc-hooks, find skills that collide or shadow each other, and find what breaks on other hosts and operating systems. Standard-library scripts, no network.

plugins.name: code-quality
plugins.description: Eight skills for keeping a codebase healthy: a review checklist, refactor planning, dead code and complexity reports, naming and error-handling audits, type coverage for Python and TypeScript, and a test gap finder.

plugins.name: compliance-evidence
plugins.description: Compliance evidence skills for Claude Code: build integrity-checked evidence packs from GitHub, AWS and Microsoft 365 exports, map them to ISO 27001 and SOC 2 control identifiers, draft auditor narratives and security questionnaire answers that cite evidence or say not assessable, map a pack to the Essential Eight maturity levels, digest vendor SOC 2 reports, ISO certificates and bridge letters, map Maester results to control identifiers, plan the evidence to collect per control as a PBC list that shows what is stale, missing or overdue, and check an ISO 27001:2022 Statement of Applicability for missing controls, unjustified decisions, status, evidence and review dates. Standard-library Python scripts read exports already on disk and make no network calls.

plugins.name: data
plugins.description: Six skills for data and API work: SQL query review, schema migration planning, CSV profiling, JSON Schema inference from samples, regex building with test cases, and OpenAPI 3 contract review.

plugins.name: debugging
plugins.description: Six skills for finding the cause of a failure: minimise a bug reproduction, cluster log lines, find flaky tests in JUnit XML, explain a stack trace, summarise a py-spy, pprof or cProfile profile, and work a memory leak checklist.

plugins.name: devops
plugins.description: Nine skills for shipping and operating software: Dockerfile hardening, GitHub Actions workflow authoring and validation, Kubernetes manifest review, Terraform review, a Terraform apply gate against a written policy, crontab diagnosis, .env key diffs, release notes from git history and a semver advisor.

plugins.name: docs
plugins.description: Six skills for writing documentation that stays accurate: README author, ADR writer, changelog keeper, onboarding doc, API docs extracted from docstrings and JSDoc, and a postmortem writer.

plugins.name: github-manager
plugins.description: Engineering manager skills that compute from exported GitHub data: a stuck-PR and review-queue digest with next actions, an iteration report with shipped, carried-over and newly opened work plus cycle time and review turnaround, a blameless incident postmortem timeline, and an issue triage digest (unlabelled, unanswered, possible duplicates, stale, popular, suggested labels). Every number and row cites the PR, issue, comment or event it came from; team level only, no per-person scoring.

plugins.name: m365-governance
plugins.description: Microsoft 365 governance skills for Claude Code: Graph permission preflight for apps and connectors, Entra ID posture review, Conditional Access gap analysis, privileged access review, guest and external sharing review, licence and service plan audit, Intune baseline check, Teams and group sprawl report, a quarterly access review pack, and a Copilot oversharing readiness score with fixes by site owner. Scripts are standard-library Python and evaluate exported Microsoft Graph JSON offline.

plugins.name: mac-maintenance
plugins.description: Mac cleanup skills: survey what takes space and memory without changing anything, remove only the caches and leftovers that programs recreate, find byte-identical duplicate files and park the obvious copies in the Trash, and find data, login items and launch agents left by uninstalled apps. Every deletion of user data is a decision the user makes from a written list.

plugins.name: repo-engineering
plugins.description: Repository engineering skills: verify documentation claims against the working tree, run an audit whose every finding cites a resolvable path:line, write AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md that hold only what code cannot say, check a README's first screen, rank untested functions and entry points, write onboarding guides only from cited facts, plan restructures from the import graph, mine ADRs from git history, run offline hygiene checks with SARIF, check release notes against the commits between two tags, sweep stale branches with delete commands printed for review, check an implementation plan for required sections and unanswered questions, and check an MCP server's server.json and package files against the MCP Registry's publish rules before publishing.

plugins.name: security-basics
plugins.description: Seven lightweight security skills for everyday development: secrets hygiene scan, npm audit and pip-audit reader, HTTP security header check, JWT inspector, CORS review, auth flow review and a security review of a diff. Agent and MCP security lives in the agent-security-skills marketplace.

plugins.name: ways-of-working
plugins.description: Thirteen ways-of-working skills that compute from files you already have: a CAB-style change record from a Terraform plan or PR export, one action ledger across meeting notes, a security exception register lint, a quarterly risk register refresh against findings exports, an RFC writer with a lifecycle lint, a one-file-per-decision log, a weekly status note from git and gh exports, a private 1:1 ledger, meeting load and focus blocks from a calendar export, a weighted vendor scorecard with a sensitivity check, a check of a team's working agreement against GitHub settings exports, a shift handover note from incident and alert exports, and one ranked do-next list from saved mail and chat exports across work and personal accounts. Standard-library scripts, no network, no rating of people.

skills.name: agent-action-timeline
skills.description: Reconstruct every action one agent or bot identity took, in time order, from saved Entra sign-in and audit logs, CloudTrail, the GitHub audit log and application logs in JSON lines, and flag bursts, unusual first-seen actions and actions outside a declared allow list. Use when asked "what did this agent do last week?", during an incident, or to see what an agent has been doing before giving it more access. Not for live monitoring or alerting, and not for investigating a human user's activity.

skills.name: agent-audit-log-integrity
skills.description: Seal an agent's audit log (JSON lines from a hook, MCP gateway or agent runtime) as a SHA-256 or HMAC hash chain, verify it later for edited, deleted, inserted or reordered lines and truncation against a stored head, and list actions the log never recorded. Use when asked "was this agent log edited?", before handing agent logs to an auditor or after an incident. Not for building the timeline (agent-action-timeline) or for log storage and retention.

skills.name: agent-kill-switch-runbook
skills.description: Prepare the kill switch runbook to stop one agent identity fast: ordered steps to disable it, end sessions, remove credentials and grants, block it at the gateway and confirm it stopped in the audit log, each with a read-only verification command. Checks every credential and assignment in the inventory has a step. Use when asked "how do we turn this agent off?", before an agent goes live, or in an incident. Not for running the steps (it changes nothing) or for offboarding a human account.

skills.name: agent-recertification
skills.description: Run the quarterly recertification of agent and workload identities: one review sheet per owner to re-attest, saying what each identity can do, when it last acted and what changed, plus a tracking CSV. Flags identities never attested, attestations older than 90 days and owners who have left. Use when asked "prepare the agent access review for this quarter" or before an audit of non-human access. Not for reviews of human users and admins (access-review-pack), listing ownerless identities (nhi-inventory) or deciding for an owner.

skills.name: connector-register
skills.description: Keep an approved register of the MCP servers, connectors and plugins your agents may use, and check every entry has an owner, purpose, data classification, permissions and review date. Compares the register with saved tools/list outputs and permission manifests to catch unregistered servers and tools and entries that are gone. Use when asked "which MCP servers are we actually running?" or before a quarterly connector review. Not for auditing an MCP server's code (mcp-server-review) or agent config files (agent-config-audit).

skills.name: credential-expiry-radar
skills.description: Find the secrets, certificates, access keys and tokens that have expired or soon will, across Entra app and Agent ID blueprint credentials, AWS IAM, GitHub fine-grained tokens and a CSV of other keys, bucketed at 7, 30 and 90 days with an action list per owner. Use when asked "which app secrets expire this month?", before a rotation sprint, or after an outage from an expired certificate or secret. Not for rotating, leaked secrets (leaked-credential-response) or what agent apps can do (entra-agent-id-review).

skills.name: entra-agent-id-review
skills.description: Review the Entra identities and service principals your AI agents use, so each one has an owner or sponsor, only the permissions it needs (including those inherited from an Agent ID blueprint), current credentials, safe redirect URIs and Conditional Access cover. Reads saved Graph exports and highlights high-risk permissions from a fixed list. Use when asked "what can our agent apps do in Entra?" or before approving an agent app. Not for human admin roles (privileged-access-review), a tenant-wide baseline (entra-posture-review) or ownerless lists (nhi-inventory).

skills.name: leaked-credential-response
skills.description: Respond to a leaked agent key, API token or secret: what it could reach, what happened after the leak time, which credentials to replace first, and an evidence folder with SHA-256 hashes. Reads the identity's inventory record and saved audit exports. Use when a key or token turns up in a commit pushed to GitHub, a chat transcript, log or ticket, or when asked "what did someone do with this leaked token?". Not for scanning code for secrets, for rotating keys itself, or for audit evidence outside an incident (evidence-pack-builder).

skills.name: nhi-inventory
skills.description: Inventory every non-human or machine identity your agents and automations run as (service principals, IAM roles and users, GitHub apps and tokens), with owner, last use, credential count and oldest credential, and flag the ownerless and the unused. Merges saved Entra (with Agent ID), AWS IAM and GitHub exports with a hand-kept register. Use when asked "which agent identities have no owner?" or when starting agent identity governance. Not for one app's Graph permissions (graph-permission-preflight), IAM policy content or human access reviews (access-review-pack).

skills.name: agent-config-audit
skills.description: Scan an AI agent configuration for risky permissions, leaked secrets, unpinned MCP servers and prompt injection in instruction files, with a bundled scanner that masks secrets. Use when asked to "check my .claude settings", to review or harden CLAUDE.md, .cursor rules, .mcp.json, hooks, skills or plugins, or before trusting a cloned repository. Not for application code (prompt-injection-review, semgrep-agentic) or MCP server code (mcp-server-review).

skills.name: agent-eval-harness
skills.description: Build a security evaluation for an agent with benign tasks, injections planted in tool results, and utility and attack success rate (ASR) scores, using a bundled standard-library runner and a policy hook. Use when asked "what is our attack success rate?", to measure how well an agent resists prompt injection, to compare defences on the same tasks, or to gate CI on ASR. Not for a manual code review without numbers (prompt-injection-review), accuracy evals of a classifier or model, or a replacement for the full AgentDojo benchmark.

skills.name: agent-session-log-review
skills.description: Review an AI agent session log, transcript or chat export for signs that prompt injection took effect, tool misuse, destructive commands, denied actions retried another way, data leaving to unknown hosts and loops, with a bundled script that normalises the log and writes a timeline of flagged events. Use when asked "what did the agent actually do in this session?", after a suspicious run, or before trusting an agent's output. Not for agent configuration (agent-config-audit), agent source code (prompt-injection-review) or CloudTrail activity (aws-agent-session-audit in aws-security).

skills.name: agent-threat-model
skills.description: Write a threat model or threat assessment for an LLM-agent system by drafting principals, tools, channels, data stores and controls in YAML from the code, running the atm analyser for STRIDE and OWASP findings, and summarising with incident precedents. Use when asked to "threat model this agent", "what could go wrong with this agent?", to map its trust boundaries and attack surface, or for a design review of an agent we are building. Not for scanning code (semgrep-agentic) or a ship decision (secure-agent-checklist).

skills.name: incident-lookup
skills.description: Look up 80 coded AI-agent security incidents from 2023 to 2026 (prompt injection, tool poisoning, exfiltration and more), mapped to OWASP Agentic and LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS techniques, and list real precedents with sources. Use when asked "has this happened before?", to find incidents that justify a control with evidence, or to "cite a precedent". Not for general CVE lookups, security news, a live threat feed or writing a threat model (agent-threat-model); it reads a daily-refreshed copy of the published dataset and falls back to a bundled snapshot offline.

skills.name: mcp-server-review
skills.description: Review an MCP server you wrote or plan to install for missing authentication, binding to a public interface, tool description poisoning, path traversal, SSRF, weak input validation and secrets in logs, then report a verdict per area with severity and file:line. Use when asked "is this MCP server safe to install?", before publishing a server, or before enabling a third-party one. Not for agent configuration files (agent-config-audit), the agent that calls the server (prompt-injection-review) or writing a new server.

skills.name: prompt-injection-review
skills.description: Trace untrusted input such as web pages, emails, tickets and tool results to consequential tool calls in agent code (sending replies, HTTP requests, shell, payments), and judge each path against provenance and approval rules. Use when asked "can this agent be prompt injected?", to find exfiltration or privilege escalation paths, or to decide where approvals belong. Not for config files (agent-config-audit) or for measuring attack success rates (agent-eval-harness).

skills.name: secure-agent-checklist
skills.description: Run a pre-ship security checklist for an LLM agent covering identity, least privilege, approvals, sandboxing, audit logging, kill switch, supply chain and evals, and report pass, fail or n.a. per item with evidence for a go or no-go sign-off. Use when asked "is this agent safe to ship?" or before deploying, releasing, open-sourcing or demoing an agent. Not for a deep component review (agent-threat-model, prompt-injection-review); it turns their evidence into a decision.

skills.name: semgrep-agentic
skills.description: Scan Python, JavaScript and TypeScript agent code with 36 Semgrep rules (model output flowing into shells, subprocess, SQL, paths or HTML, user input in system prompts, MCP servers without auth, leaked provider keys), with a bundled offline fallback, and triage the hits. Use when asked to "scan this agent for security issues", to add agent rules to CI, or for the code step of an agent security audit. Not for general SAST, other languages or runtime behaviour.

skills.name: tool-approval-gate-audit
skills.description: Find every tool a Python agent's model can call, decide which have consequential side effects (deleting files, sending email, cloud writes), and check whether a human approves each one through a deterministic gate that cannot fail open, with gaps reported per tool at file and line. Use when asked "which of my agent's tools run without approval?", before shipping an OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, crewAI or FastMCP agent, or to check needs_approval and interrupt gates. Not for tracing injected input to tools (prompt-injection-review) or a whole-system threat model (agent-threat-model).

skills.name: agent-safe-aws-access
skills.description: Plan least-privilege AWS access for an AI coding agent from a short spec, producing the trust policy, task-scoped permissions, a permission boundary, an SCP backstop, the assume-role command and a kill switch, or review an existing agent role against the same rules. Use when asked to "give my coding agent access to our AWS account", when an agent will deploy or run anything there, or when auditing an agent role. Not for human IAM users (iam-least-privilege-review) or organization-wide SCP design (scp-guardrails).

skills.name: aws-account-audit
skills.description: Audit one AWS account for security gaps by collecting inventory with read-only aws CLI commands and evaluating 17 checks offline (root MFA and keys, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, S3 public access, open security groups, old keys, admin policies, encryption), with severity, evidence and a fix per finding. Use when asked "is this account secure?", to baseline or check an account, before handing over an account or after an incident. Not for compliance evidence rows (aws-identity-and-logging-evidence), organization design (landing-zone-blast-radius) or deep IAM analysis (iam-least-privilege-review).

skills.name: aws-agent-session-audit
skills.description: Audit what an AI coding agent did in an AWS account and which permissions it never needed, from a saved CloudTrail export of the agent's role session: actions by service, writes versus reads, calls outside a declared allow list, logging tampering, destructive and IAM calls, resources touched and errors. Use when asked "what did the agent do according to CloudTrail?", after an agent session or before widening its role. Not for reviewing policy text (iam-least-privilege-review), planning a new agent role (agent-safe-aws-access) or local tool calls (agent-session-log-review).

skills.name: aws-incident-response-runbook
skills.description: Write a filled-in AWS incident response runbook for a leaked access key, a compromised EC2 instance, a public S3 bucket, suspicious IAM activity, ransomware that deletes S3 objects or EBS volumes, or crypto-mining: read-only inventory first, containment commands that each need confirmation, evidence, recovery and templates; a triage mode picks the scenario from GuardDuty findings. Use when asked "we leaked an AWS key, what now?", when a GuardDuty finding needs a response plan or to prepare runbooks early. Not for a posture backlog (security-hub-triage) or routine audits (aws-account-audit).

skills.name: aws-spend-guardrails
skills.description: Generate AWS Budgets, a Cost Anomaly Detection monitor and a sandbox SCP that denies expensive services (large GPU instances, SageMaker and similar), then check an exported Cost Explorer report for spikes. Use when asked to "stop runaway AWS spend", when setting cost alerts, protecting sandbox or agent accounts from a bill that grows overnight, or explaining a cost spike. Not for rightsizing or savings recommendations, or a full sandbox OU pack (sandbox-account-guardrail-pack).

skills.name: iam-least-privilege-review
skills.description: Review AWS IAM policies offline, from policy files or a get-account-authorization-details export, for over-broad permissions and privilege-escalation paths (admin, wildcards, unscoped iam:PassRole, NotAction in Allow, known escalation combinations), ranked by severity with a tightened policy per document. Use when asked "is this IAM policy least privilege?", before approving a permissions change, or after an audit flags an admin policy on a role. Not for SCPs (scp-guardrails), bucket or key policies, or planning an agent's role (agent-safe-aws-access).

skills.name: landing-zone-blast-radius
skills.description: Design an AWS Organizations landing zone with one account per workload and environment, and show what a compromise of each account can reach. A bundled script turns a workload list into the OU tree, account names, foundation accounts and where SCP guardrails attach. Use when asked "how should we split our AWS accounts?", when planning a new organization, splitting a shared account or adding a workload. Not for auditing an existing account (aws-account-audit) or writing SCP JSON (scp-guardrails).

skills.name: preventive-control-mapper
skills.description: Turn failing Security Hub controls and Prowler checks (S3, EC2, IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, RDS and more) into the preventive controls that stop the same misconfiguration coming back: an SCP statement, an account or declarative-policy setting, an IaC check, plus the AWS Config rule that detects a regression. Offline, from saved exports. Use when asked "how do we stop this finding coming back?" or to move from fixing findings to preventing them. Not for deciding what to fix first (security-hub-triage), linting an SCP (scp-guardrails) or checking one account (aws-account-audit).

skills.name: sandbox-account-guardrail-pack
skills.description: Generate a guardrail pack for an AWS sandbox OU where engineers and AI agents experiment: SCPs that pass the bundled size checks (region allowlist, IMDSv2, no root, protected logging), AWS Budgets, a checklist for new sandbox accounts and a tag-based auto-expiry design. Use when asked to "set up a safe sandbox account", or when creating or tightening a sandbox or training OU. Not for production OUs or linting an existing SCP (scp-guardrails), runaway spend alerts on their own (aws-spend-guardrails) or checking an existing account (aws-account-audit), and it never runs the cleanup.

skills.name: scp-guardrails
skills.description: Write, review and lint AWS Organizations service control policies: build SCPs from a short spec (region allowlist, break-glass roles, protected logging, no root user, IMDSv2, no public S3 ACLs) under the SCP character limit, and lint any SCP for Allow statements, region denies that break global services, NotAction misuse and size. Use when asked "why did our region SCP break IAM?", to write a service control policy, or to lint a guardrail SCP before you attach it to an OU. Not for IAM identity policies (iam-least-privilege-review) or organization design (landing-zone-blast-radius).

skills.name: security-hub-triage
skills.description: Turn a Security Hub or GuardDuty findings backlog into an owner-assigned next-actions list, offline from exports. A bundled script drops resolved and suppressed findings, groups the rest by severity, control and resource, assigns owners from rules and orders actions by severity and reach. Use when asked "what do we fix first in Security Hub?", for a weekly security review, or to route findings to teams. Not for running new checks (aws-account-audit) or responding to one active incident (aws-incident-response-runbook).

skills.name: compaction-loss-check
skills.description: Check each compaction in a Claude Code session transcript: trigger, tokens before and after, time since the last user message, and whether the summary kept the standing rules the user gave, the files edited, branches and pull requests created and open to-dos. Prints a re-state list and a paste-ready recap. Use when asked "what did compaction forget?" or after a session ignored an earlier instruction. Not for what loads on every turn (context-budget-audit) or token totals (session-usage-ledger).

skills.name: context-budget-audit
skills.description: Audit what a Claude Code project puts in context on every turn (CLAUDE.md and its imports, AGENTS.md, rules files, skill descriptions, MCP tool schemas from saved tools/list output, hooks), estimate the tokens, rank the biggest items and flag duplicates and stale sections. Use when asked "why is my context so full?", when sessions compact early, or before adding more skills or servers. Not for measuring a live session's usage or for editing a skill's own instructions.

skills.name: hook-author
skills.description: Write and test a Claude Code hook with cc-hooks: pick the event and the decision (block, warn, allow or modify) from a table, scaffold the hook, its fixtures, a pytest file and the settings block from a short spec, then prove it with cc-hooks test. Use when asked "add a hook that blocks this command", to warn on risky edits, or to turn a team rule into a check that runs every time. Not for permission rules alone (use permissions-builder) or hooks for other agents.

skills.name: permissions-builder
skills.description: Build a least-privilege .claude/settings.json permission set from what a project actually needs: generate MCP rules with claude-mcp-allow, merge them with your own allow, ask and deny lists, put deny first, diff against the current file, then test the result with claude-perm-sim against the commands the team runs. Use when asked "set up permissions for this repo" or to stop approving the same prompts. Not for sandboxing or for organisation-wide managed settings.

skills.name: sandbox-config-review
skills.description: Review a Claude Code project's sandbox settings across user, project, local and managed scopes, show what the operating system actually enforces around Bash commands, and flag what leaves it open: sandbox off, fail-open, the unsandboxed retry, broad excludedCommands, wildcard domains, readable credentials and loosening values a cloned repository ships. Use when asked "is my sandbox actually locked down?" or before trusting auto-allow. Not for permission rules (use permissions-builder) or for containers and VMs.

skills.name: session-usage-ledger
skills.description: Add up the API usage recorded in Claude Code session transcripts per day, session, model and project (calls, input, output, cache reads, 5-minute and 1-hour cache writes, cache-hit ratio, first-call size, subagent share) and compare two periods to show which part moved. Use when asked "why did my usage jump this week?" or whether cache writes are 5-minute when 1 hour was expected. Not for what loads on every turn (context-budget-audit) or for plan quotas, which transcripts do not hold.

skills.name: shell-slip-audit
skills.description: Pair every Bash and PowerShell call in Claude Code session transcripts with its result and count the calls that failed because of the shell: zsh glob, equals and syntax errors, bash syntax sent to PowerShell, commands cut at the Windows length limit, including silent failures the call did not mark as errors. Use when asked "why do my Bash commands keep failing under zsh?" or for a CLAUDE.md rule against these slips. Not for permission prompts (unattended-run-preflight) or the sandbox (sandbox-config-review).

skills.name: skill-collision-check
skills.description: Find installed skills that share a name, shadow each other or overlap so much in description that the wrong one gets picked, across personal, project, managed, plugin and copied folders, and say which one wins. Use when asked "why did the wrong skill run?", after installing a plugin or skill pack, or before choosing a name for a new skill. Not for linting one description (use skill-description-linter) or for measuring triggering against prompts (use skill-trigger-eval).

skills.name: skill-description-linter
skills.description: Lint the front matter of your SKILL.md files so each skill is listed and picked correctly: double-quoted description under 600 characters, a verb first, a quoted trigger phrase, Use when and Not for sentences, name equal to the folder, strict-YAML safety and a Limits section, with --fix for the quoting. Use when asked "why does my skill not trigger?", before publishing skills, or in CI. Not for testing which prompts trigger a skill (use skill-trigger-eval) or for reviewing third-party skills.

skills.name: skill-portability-check
skills.description: Check a skill folder for what breaks on other hosts and operating systems: unquoted YAML colons, hard-coded home paths, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with no fallback, GNU-only or BSD-only shell, Python open calls without encoding, POSIX-only calls, Windows path separators, CRLF and symlinks, with a fix hint per file. Use when asked "will this skill work on Windows?", before publishing a skill, or in CI. Not for security review (use skill-supply-chain-review) or description wording.

skills.name: skill-supply-chain-review
skills.description: Review a third-party skill or plugin before you install it: run skill-scan-gate on the folder, lock it with cc-plugin-lock, read every script for network and shell use with a bundled offline inventory, and write a one-page verdict. Use when asked "is this skill safe to install?", before adding a marketplace or plugin, or when a locked plugin changed. Not for skills you are writing yourself (use skill-description-linter and skill-portability-check) and not a malware sandbox.

skills.name: skill-trigger-eval
skills.description: Measure whether a skill's description triggers on the prompts it should and stays quiet on the ones it should not, using a labelled prompt set and transparent lexical scoring, and compare two description versions by precision and recall. Use when asked "will this description trigger?", before and after rewriting a description, or to find two skills competing for one prompt. Not for predicting the host's real choice, which a model makes; this is a proxy.

skills.name: subagent-tool-scope-review
skills.description: Review every Claude Code subagent file for the tools it can actually reach: agents with no tools line inherit every built-in and MCP tool, lookalike fields such as allowed-tools are ignored, and reviewers that can write or run a shell. Proposes a narrower tools line. Use when asked "which of my subagents can use the GitHub MCP tools?", before adding an MCP server or after installing a plugin with agents. Not for permission rules (permissions-builder) or for skills (skill-supply-chain-review).

skills.name: unattended-run-preflight
skills.description: Replay the tool calls of a Claude Code run (a session log or a list) against the permission rules in your settings files and show which calls would stop a scheduled task, routine, CI job or claude -p run on a prompt or a deny rule, with the narrowest allow rule for each. Use when asked "why does my scheduled task stall on permission prompts?" or before running a prompt unattended.
